titleTh: ตกลงเรื่องเพื่อนมาค้างที่ห้อง
scenarioSentences: You share an apartment with Owen.
His friend Leo stays over most nights.
Leo often eats your food.
You have no rules about guests yet.
You raise it with Owen tonight.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Owen, can we talk about Leo? He's stayed here almost every night this month.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Is it a problem? He's between apartments right now.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The bathroom's always busy in the morning, and my food keeps disappearing.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: That must have been him. Sorry, I'll replace it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'd rather we had a clear rule, though. Guests two nights a week at most?

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: Could we make it three while he looks for a place?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Three is fine for two weeks, as long as you tell me first.

dialogue.speaker: Owen
dialogue.text: That's fair. After that, it's two nights, and I'll always ask you first.

titleEn: Getting a bank late fee removed
titleTh: ขอให้ธนาคารยกเลิกค่าปรับจ่ายช้า
scenarioSentences: Your bank charged you a late fee.
You tried to pay on the due date.
However, the bank's website was down.
Mr. Ashford works at the customer desk.
You visit him about the fee.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi. I've been charged a late fee, but I don't think it's fair.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ashford
dialogue.text: I see your payment arrived a day late. I could reduce the fee by half.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd rather not pay anything. I tried to pay on time, but your website was down.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ashford
dialogue.text: We did have a system problem that night. Do you have any evidence?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I took a screenshot of the error message. It shows the time.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ashford
dialogue.text: That's clear enough. In that case, I'll remove the whole fee.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you. Will the late payment affect my credit record?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Ashford
dialogue.text: No, I'll delete it from your record as well. You'll get a letter confirming it.

titleEn: Planning a wedding speech with a friend
titleTh: วางแผนกล่าวสุนทรพจน์งานแต่งพี่ชาย
scenarioSentences: Your brother is getting married next month.
He has asked you to give a speech.
You are nervous about speaking in public.
Your friend Matteo gave one last year.
You ask him for advice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm giving the speech at my brother's wedding. How long should it be?

dialogue.speaker: Matteo
dialogue.text: Under five minutes. Otherwise, people stop listening, especially after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd like to tell the story of how he met Anna.

dialogue.speaker: Matteo
dialogue.text: Good. It's also worth adding one funny story from your childhood.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd rather not embarrass him in front of her family, though.

dialogue.speaker: Matteo
dialogue.text: Then pick something silly, not embarrassing, like his terrible cooking.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. And how should I end it?

dialogue.speaker: Matteo
dialogue.text: Thank both families and the guests, then ask everyone to raise their glasses.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. I'll write a short, funny draft and read it to you on Friday.

dialogue.speaker: Matteo
dialogue.text: Sounds good. Practice it out loud a few times first.

titleTh: วางแผนงานวันเปิดบ้านของโรงเรียน
scenarioSentences: Your school has an open day on Saturday.
You are leading the student helpers.
Last year's tour groups were too big.
Mr. Byrne is the teacher in charge.
You meet him to plan the day.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Mr. Byrne, last year's tours had about thirty parents each. Many couldn't hear the guides.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Byrne
dialogue.text: I remember the complaints. What would you suggest this year?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: If we had groups of ten, everyone could ask questions.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Byrne
dialogue.text: That would mean three times as many guides. Do we have enough students?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Twelve have signed up so far. I could ask the drama club for more.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Byrne
dialogue.text: As long as each guide gets training on Thursday, that's fine with me.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And should the tours start every fifteen minutes instead of every hour?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Byrne
dialogue.text: Yes, that's more flexible for families. Try to find eight more helpers by Wednesday.

titleEn: Choosing between the beach and mountains
titleTh: เลือกเที่ยวทะเลหรือภูเขากับเพื่อน
scenarioSentences: You and Arjun are planning a winter vacation.
You have one week off in December.
Arjun wants to go to the beach.
You prefer the mountains, but money is tight.
You discuss it at lunch.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Beach or mountains? We need to decide soon, or prices will go up.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Beach, definitely. I just want to lie in the sun for a week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I get that, but beach hotels in December cost almost twice as much.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Really? How much is the mountain place you found?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: About forty dollars a night, and it has a kitchen, so we could cook.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: That's much cheaper. But I'd be bored if we only went hiking.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: There's a lake with boats and a hot spring nearby. You'd love it.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Fine, you've convinced me. As long as we book soon, I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: If we book before Friday, there's a fifteen percent discount.

dialogue.speaker: Arjun
dialogue.text: Then let's book it tonight.

titleTh: แจ้งปัญหาทางข้ามถนนอันตราย
scenarioSentences: Your sister's school is on a busy road.
Cars drive fast there every morning.
There is no safe place to cross.
Mr. Clarke works at the city council.
You call him to report the problem.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello. I'm calling about the road outside the primary school. Cars drive dangerously fast there.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clarke
dialogue.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Has anyone been hurt?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not yet, but a boy was nearly hit last week. Children need a proper crossing.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clarke
dialogue.text: I understand, but we can't approve a crossing without evidence of the traffic.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How would you get that? I'd hate to wait until there's an accident.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clarke
dialogue.text: We'll do a traffic survey this month to measure speed and the number of cars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And if the results are bad, will you build a crossing?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Clarke
dialogue.text: Probably, though it depends on the budget. I'll email you the results either way.

titleTh: เปรียบเทียบแล็ปท็อปสองรุ่นก่อนซื้อ
scenarioSentences: You need a laptop for your studies.
You have a budget of eight hundred dollars.
Two models in the shop look good.
Mr. Kwan, the shop assistant, comes over.
You ask him to compare them.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could you explain the difference between these two laptops?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kwan
dialogue.text: The silver one is lighter, but the black one is more powerful.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I carry it to class daily, so weight matters. What's the price difference?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kwan
dialogue.text: The silver one is six hundred. The black one is nine hundred.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's over my budget. Is the silver one fast enough for video editing?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kwan
dialogue.text: Not really, unless you add more memory. That's an extra hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: So seven hundred in total, still cheaper than the black one.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Kwan
dialogue.text: And we can install the memory today, so you'd take it home tonight.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: In that case, I'll take the silver one with the extra memory.

titleTh: แจ้งกระเป๋าเดินทางหายที่สนามบิน
scenarioSentences: You have just landed after a long flight.
Your suitcase never appeared on the belt.
You have a job interview tomorrow morning.
Ms. Petrov works at the baggage desk.
You go to her for help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: My suitcase didn't arrive, and I have a job interview tomorrow at nine.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Petrov
dialogue.text: I'm sorry. It seems it was left behind at your last stop.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: My suit's in it. When will it get here?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Petrov
dialogue.text: It'll be on tomorrow's first flight, so we can deliver it to your hotel by noon.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's too late. What am I supposed to wear?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Petrov
dialogue.text: You can buy what you need tonight, and we'll pay you back.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Is there a limit? A decent shirt and shoes aren't cheap.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Petrov
dialogue.text: Up to two hundred dollars, as long as you keep the receipts for your claim.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's fine. Please call me when the bag's on its way.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Petrov
dialogue.text: I will. Here's your reference number.

titleTh: แก้ปัญหาห้องประชุมถูกจองซ้ำ
scenarioSentences: Your team meets at two o'clock today.
You booked the big meeting room.
Your coworker Gemma says she booked it too.
Her team is already setting up inside.
You need to solve this quickly.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Gemma, I think there's been a mistake. I booked this room for two o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: Gemma
dialogue.text: So did I. The system must have let us both book it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's annoying. My team has eight people, and two are joining from home.

dialogue.speaker: Gemma
dialogue.text: Mine's twelve people, and we're showing a new design to a client in person.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then you should probably keep it. We could have our meeting online instead.

dialogue.speaker: Gemma
dialogue.text: Are you sure? I'd be happy to give you the room another day if you need it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Actually, Thursday would help. We have a big planning session that morning.

dialogue.speaker: Gemma
dialogue.text: It's yours. I'll also report the booking problem so it doesn't happen again.

titleEn: Deciding whether to repair an old car
titleTh: ตัดสินใจว่าจะซ่อมรถเก่าดีไหม
scenarioSentences: Your car is twelve years old.
It failed its safety check this week.
Mr. Russo, your mechanic, has looked at it.
The repair is expensive.
You are not sure it is worth it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How bad is it, Mr. Russo?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Russo
dialogue.text: The brakes need replacing, and there's an oil leak. About nine hundred dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Nine hundred? The car's only worth two thousand.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Russo
dialogue.text: I know. If it were my car, I'd fix it and sell it next year.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Why not sell it now?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Russo
dialogue.text: With bad brakes, you'd get much less. And a reliable replacement costs at least eight thousand.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I can't afford that yet. Could you do the brakes now and the leak later?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Russo
dialogue.text: Sure. The leak can wait a few months, so that's about five hundred today.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then please fix the brakes. I'll sell it next year.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Russo
dialogue.text: Sensible. It'll be ready on Wednesday.
